problems.title: Kick at 9,800 ft: kill sheet basics
given: Slow circulating rate pressure SCR = 600 psi
problems.find: Formation pressure, kill mud weight (KMW), initial and final circulating pressures.

steps.h: Hydrostatic pressure of the current mud

steps.note: In practice round up to 11.3 ppg.

problems.final: P<sub>f</sub> ≈ 5,750 psi, KMW ≈ 11.3 ppg, ICP = 1,050 psi, FCP ≈ 652 psi.

problems.title: Weighting up with barite
problems.find: Sacks of barite needed and the volume increase.
problems.final: About 563 sacks (56,300 lb) of barite; the system grows by about 38 bbl, so check pit space.

problems.title: Equivalent circulating density
given: Fracture gradient at the shoe = 0.60 psi/ft
problems.find: ECD, and whether it stays below the fracture gradient.

steps.note: A margin this small is risky: reduce the flow rate or improve hole cleaning.

problems.final: ECD ≈ 11.45 ppg, only about 0.09 ppg below the fracture gradient.

problems.title: Porosity and water saturation from logs
problems.find: Density porosity and water saturation. Is it pay if the S<sub>w</sub> cutoff is 50%?

problems.title: Vogel IPR for a saturated reservoir
given: Average reservoir pressure p̄<sub>r</sub> = 2,500 psi (= bubblepoint)
Test: q = 600 STB/d at p<sub>wf</sub> = 1,800 psi
problems.find: q<sub>max</sub> (AOF) and the rate at p<sub>wf</sub> = 1,000 psi.

problems.title: Buildup test: permeability and skin
given: q = 250 STB/d, B = 1.15 rb/STB, μ = 0.9 cp
h = 40 ft, φ = 0.18, c<sub>t</sub> = 1.5 × 10<sup>−5</sup> psi<sup>−1</sup>, r<sub>w</sub> = 0.33 ft
problems.find: Permeability, skin and the pressure drop due to skin.

eq: s = 1.151 [ (p<sub>1hr</sub> − p<sub>wf</sub>)/m − log( k / (φ μ c<sub>t</sub> r<sub>w</sub>²) ) + 3.23 ]

problems.final: k ≈ 30 mD, s ≈ 9.2 (damaged); about 280 psi is lost to skin, so a stimulation candidate.

problems.title: Exponential decline to economic limit
problems.find: Nominal decline rate, time to abandonment and remaining reserves.
problems.final: D ≈ 22.3%/yr, about 10.3 years of life, ≈ 1.47 MMSTB.

problems.title: Seismic depth and resolution
problems.final: Target ≈ 2,520 m; beds thinner than about 25 m will not resolve.

problems.title: Reflection coefficient of a gas sand
given: Gas sand: ρ = 2.10 g/cc, V = 2,500 m/s (below)
problems.find: Reflection coefficient at the top of the sand.
problems.final: R ≈ −0.12: a negative (soft) reflection, typical of a gas sand under shale.

problems.title: Test report: API gravity and GOR
problems.final: 35 °API light oil with a GOR of 800 scf/STB.

problems.title: Designing underbalance for TCP
given: Reservoir pressure = 4,200 psi at 8,000 ft TVD
problems.find: Density of the cushion fluid filling the tubing, and the number of shots.

steps.h: Fluid density for a full column

problems.final: ≈ 8.9 ppg cushion (or a partial column of a denser fluid); 420 shots.

problems.title: Tubing volume for a bullhead kill
problems.find: Tubing volume and pumping time to displace it.
problems.final: ≈ 58 bbl to the perforations, about 19 minutes at 3 bpm.

problems.title: Mobility ratio before and after polymer

problems.final: Water occupies about 60% of the pipe at that depth (the water cut is lower because oil slips past).

problems.title: Adsorbed gas from a Langmuir isotherm

projects.title: Mud and casing program for a three-section well
projects.brief: You are given pore-pressure and fracture-gradient data for a 12,000 ft vertical well. Plan casing seats and mud weights section by section.
tasks: Plot pore pressure and fracture gradient (ppg) against depth.
Choose casing setting depths with a 0.5 ppg trip margin and a 0.5 ppg kick margin.
Pick a mud type and weight for each section and justify it.
Calculate the hydrostatic pressure at each casing point.

projects.title: Quick-look log interpretation
projects.brief: Use the readings below (clean-to-shaly sand) to find pay. GR<sub>clean</sub> = 20 API, GR<sub>shale</sub> = 120 API, ρ<sub>ma</sub> = 2.65, ρ<sub>f</sub> = 1.0, R<sub>w</sub> = 0.05 Ω·m, a = 1, m = n = 2.
tasks: Compute I<sub>GR</sub> (use it as V<sub>sh</sub>), density porosity and Archie S<sub>w</sub> for each depth.
Apply cutoffs: V<sub>sh</sub> < 0.4, φ > 0.10, S<sub>w</sub> < 0.5.
Identify the likely oil–water contact.
deliverables: Table of V<sub>sh</sub>, φ, S<sub>w</sub>, pay flag
projects.check: At 5,020 ft: V<sub>sh</sub> = 0.15, φ ≈ 0.212, S<sub>w</sub> ≈ 0.157 → pay. At 5,040 ft, φ ≈ 0.206 but S<sub>w</sub> ≈ 0.69 → water.

projects.title: Nodal analysis in a spreadsheet
projects.brief: Build the IPR (Vogel) and a simple tubing curve, and find the operating point before and after an ESP.
data: p̄<sub>r</sub> = 2,800 psi (saturated), test 700 STB/d at 2,000 psi
An ESP adds 900 psi at the pump
tasks: Compute q<sub>max</sub> and tabulate the IPR from 0 to 2,800 psi.
Tabulate the outflow curve and find the intersection.
Shift the outflow curve down by 900 psi and find the new rate.

projects.title: Interpret a buildup
projects.brief: Shut-in data from an oil well after t<sub>p</sub> = 72 h at 300 STB/d (B = 1.2, μ = 1.1 cp, h = 25 ft, φ = 0.2, c<sub>t</sub> = 1.2 × 10<sup>−5</sup>, r<sub>w</sub> = 0.35 ft, p<sub>wf</sub> = 2,150 psi).
tasks: Make a Horner plot and pick the straight line.
Compute k, skin and p*.
Make a log-log Δp and derivative plot and identify flow regimes.

projects.title: Infill well economics
projects.brief: Decide whether an infill well is worth drilling under a service contract.
data: Oil price $70/bbl, OPEX $12/bbl, government share 60% of net proceeds
tasks: Draw the cash-flow diagram.
Compute yearly production, revenue, costs and contractor cash flow.
Compute NPV, IRR and payout.
Run a sensitivity at $55 and $85/bbl.

projects.title: EOR screening study
projects.brief: Rank EOR methods for a mature waterflooded field.
data: Oil 24 °API, μ<sub>o</sub> = 12 cp at reservoir conditions
Sandstone, formation water salinity 30,000 ppm, current water cut 92%
tasks: Compare the field with published screening ranges for thermal, CO<sub>2</sub>, polymer, surfactant and low-salinity methods.
Compute the mobility ratio of the waterflood and with polymer (μ<sub>w</sub> 0.4 → 8 cp).
Rank the top two methods and list the data you still need.

projects.title: Completion for a sandy gas well
projects.brief: Design the completion for a weak, unconsolidated gas sand.
data: Depth 7,200 ft TVD, P<sub>res</sub> = 3,300 psi, 30 ft net pay
tasks: Choose open-hole or cased-hole and the sand control method (screen, gravel pack, frac pack).
Select charge type, shot density and phasing.
Specify completion fluid density for 200 psi overbalance.
Sketch the completion schematic with barriers.

exam_tips: Write the given, the find and the units before touching the calculator.
Box your final answer with its unit; check it is physically reasonable (for example, Z between 0.3 and 2, S<sub>w</sub> between 0 and 1).
For well control always use TVD; for volumes use MD.
For any engineering economy problem, draw the cash-flow diagram first.
